hints.content:
$g$ is increasing in an interval where as $x$ increases, $g(x)$ also increases.

Visually, this is where the graph is going upwards as we go from left to right.



[[☃ image 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane. The x-axis scales by one, and the y-axis scales by ten. The graph of y equals f of x is a continuous curve. From left to right, it passes through the negative five, negative fifty, and the x-intercept negative four point four, zero. It continues to increase through the point negative four, twenty until a local maximum at negative three point five, twenty-eight. Then it decreases through the point three, twenty and the x-intercept negative two point two, zero until a local minimum at negative one, negative twenty. Then it increases through the origin and the point one, forty-five until a local maximum at two point four, ninety, Then it decreases through the x-intercept three point six, zero. All values are estimates. The function is highlighted from x equals five to x equals three point five and from x equals negative one to x equals two point four.

hints.content:
Now we can check each option:

Interval | Is $g$ increasing on the interval?
:-: | :-:
$-4.5<x<-4$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$-1<x<0.5$ | $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
$1.5<x<2$ |  $\greenD{\text{Yes!}}$
